units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
I must live differently, mother. That is why I must leave you. I will not have you looking on at it.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: My unhappy boy! But, Oswald, while you are so ill as this--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: If it were only the illness, I should stay with you, mother, you may be sure; for you are the best friend I have in the world.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, indeed I am, Oswald; am I not?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Wanders restlessly about.
But it's all the torment, the gnawing remorse--and then, the great, killing dread. Oh--that awful dread!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Walking after him.
Dread? What dread? What do you mean?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, you mustn't ask me any more. I don't know. I can't describe it.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Goes over to the right and pulls the bell.
What is it you want?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I want my boy to be happy--that is what I want. He sha'n't go on brooding over things.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: To REGINA, who appears at the door:.
More champagne--a large bottle.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: REGINA goes.
Mother!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Do you think we don't know how to live here at home?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Isn't she splendid to look at? How beautifully she's built! And so thoroughly healthy!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Sits by the table.
Sit down, Oswald; let us talk quietly together.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Sits.
I daresay you don't know, mother, that I owe Regina some reparation.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: You!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: For a bit of thoughtlessness, or whatever you like to call it--very innocent, at any rate. When I was home last time--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Well?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She used often to ask me about Paris, and I used to tell her one thing and another. Then I recollect I happened to say to her one day, "Shouldn't you like to go there yourself?"
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Well?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I saw her face flush, and then she said, "Yes, I should like it of all things." "Ah, well," I replied, "it might perhaps be managed"--or something like that.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: And then?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Of course I had forgotten all about it; but the day before yesterday I happened to ask her whether she was glad I was to stay at home so long--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: And then she gave me such a strange look, and asked, "But what's to become of my trip to Paris?"
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Her trip!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: And so it came out that she had taken the thing seriously; that she had been thinking of me the whole time, and had set to work to learn French--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: So that was why--!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Mother--when I saw that fresh, lovely, splendid girl standing there before me--till then I had hardly noticed her--but when she stood there as though with open arms ready to receive me--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oswald!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: --then it flashed upon me that in her lay my salvation; for I saw that she was full of the joy of life.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Starts.
The joy of life? Can there be salvation in that?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: From the dining room, with a bottle of champagne.
I'm sorry to have been so long, but I had to go to the cellar.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Places the bottle on the table.
And now bring another glass.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Looks at him in surprise.
